title: Getting GLM 5.2 running on my slow computer
claim: Show HN: Getting GLM 5.2 running on my slow computer
why_good: A Show HN write-up on squeezing GLM-5.2 onto a slow machine — great signal that 'run big models on weak hardware' resonates, but it's a post, not a product.
value: Privacy-bound professionals (lawyers, clinicians, defence-adjacent) and the uncensored-model crowd, who already buy hardware to avoid the cloud; the sale is a paid desktop app, not tokens.
risk: Free incumbents (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) can absorb tiered offload at any time, and the speed ceiling keeps the audience small.

zh.claim: Show HN: 在我的慢电脑上把 GLM 5.2 跑起来。
zh.why_good: 一篇把 GLM-5.2 塞进慢机器的 Show HN 记录——很好地证明弱硬件跑大模型有共鸣,但它是帖子不是产品。
zh.value: 受合规约束的专业人士（律师、医生、涉密相关）与无审查模型用户，他们本来就在为「不上云」买硬件；卖的是付费桌面应用，不是 token。
zh.risk: 免费在位者（Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp）随时能补上分层卸载，而速度天花板决定了受众规模有限。
zh.hook: 那些不肯把自己的东西传到别人服务器上、又没法为一台 768GB 内存的云主机买单的人，只能在 7B 玩具和永远交不完的 API 账单之间二选一。
zh.does: 纯 C、零引擎依赖的推理引擎，把 SSD、内存、显存当作一整套内存层级来调度，于是 744B–2.8T 的 MoE 模型（GLM-5.2、Inkling、Kimi K3）能跑在消费级和混合硬件上。每个模型家族一个 C 文件，共用 `coli chat / serve / web`，仪表盘能看到 19,456 个专家分别驻留在哪一层。
zh.gap: 只有极客用得了：这是一套要你自己编译、摆放、调参的 C 引擎，而一台普通 32GB 笔记本的主人根本无从知道自己到底能跑哪个前沿模型、几 tok/s、要付出多少 SSD 寿命。
zh.counter: 1–5 tok/s 是演示不是工作流——HN 帖子里读者自己就在问「5 tok/s 能干什么」。Ollama 和 LM Studio 占着「本地模型 + 好看的窗口」这个位置，一个小版本就能加上分层卸载，llama.cpp 已经有 MoE offload；API 价格每便宜一个月，把 744B 留在家里的理由就薄一分。而且你要卖的产品，诚实的免责声明是「会磨损用户的 SSD」。
zh.differentiator: 别再写引擎。在别人的引擎上做诚实的能力层：读一遍机器就告诉你「GLM-5.2 int4，约 3 tok/s，每小时约写入 40GB」，然后默认带磨损上限地一键装好——卖给那批已经明说「愿意用速度换掌控」的隐私与无审查用户。
zh.consumer_angle: 普通人那侧的产品是「我这台电脑到底能跑多大的模型、代价是什么」——一个把速度和 SSD 磨损如实写在前面的一键本地运行器，而不是又一个引擎。

hook: People who refuse to send their work to someone else's server — and cannot justify renting a 768 GB cloud box — are stuck choosing between a 7B toy and a permanent API bill.
pick_reason: The project is a post rather than a product, lacking a clear monetizable offering.

voices.quote: doing the math on what it costs to rent a 768GB+ RAM AWS system with 40+ high performance CPU cores makes it very unappealing to pay for 12, 24, 36 months of it
…[people who will not] submit everything they do to an off site service, or let their content be used for unknown training purposes, and will tolerate slowness at 1 to 10 tok/s as a tradeoff.

The page has an SSD wear warning. I use desktop PCs that I build from components so I can replace the SSD, but what do users with soldered SSD do? Just avoid these applications or forge ahead disregarding the possible early burnout of their storage?

does: A pure-C inference engine with zero engine dependencies that treats SSD, RAM and VRAM as one managed memory hierarchy, so 744B–2.8T MoE models (GLM-5.2, Inkling, Kimi K3) run on consumer and mixed hardware. One C file per model family behind the same `coli chat / serve / web` front end, with a dashboard showing which of the 19,456 experts are resident on which tier.
gap: Only geeks can use it: it is a C engine you build, place and tune, and nothing tells the owner of an ordinary 32 GB laptop which frontier model their machine can actually hold, at what tok/s, or how much SSD life it will cost them.
counter: At 1–5 tok/s this is a demonstration, not a workflow — the thread's own readers ask what 5 tok/s is even good for. Ollama and LM Studio own the 'local model with a window' slot and can add tiered offload in a point release, llama.cpp already ships MoE offload, and each month of cheaper API tokens thins the reason to keep a 744B model at home. You would also be shipping a product whose honest disclaimer is that it wears out the customer's SSD.
differentiator: Do not write another engine. Ship the honest capability layer on top of one: a profiler that reads the machine and says 'GLM-5.2 int4, ~3 tok/s, ~40 GB of SSD writes per hour', then one-click installs it with wear limits on by default — aimed at the privacy-and-uncensored crowd who have already said they will trade speed for control.
consumer_angle: The ordinary-person product is 'which big model can MY computer run, and what does it cost my hardware' — a one-click local runner with honest speed and SSD-wear numbers, not another engine.
